newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians burn Macedonian flag in Tirana protest.
newsitem.headline: Albanians burn Macedonian flag in Tirana protest.

text.p: Hundreds of Albanians demonstrated in Tirana on Saturday, burning a Macedonian flag to protest over police treatment of ethnic Albanians in neighbouring Macedonia.
Some 200 to 300 youngsters, mainly students from Macedonia and the Yugoslav province of Kosovo, marched from the university to Skanderbeg Square and the main embassies compound.

Watched by police, they shouted slogans in support of their compatriots in the former Yugoslav republic, sang patriotic songs along the main boulevard and burned a Macedonian flag outside the embassy. Some leaders of Albania's Socialist and Democratic parties attended the rally.

Two Albanians were shot dead, about 53 seriously injured and around 400 detained in rioting on Wednesday in Gostivar, western Macedonia, when police removed the Albanian national flag from outside the town hall under a new law which limits the flying of flags to special occasions.
Last Thursday Albania summoned the Macedonian ambassador to protest over police treatment of ethnic Albanians in Macedonia.

Tension between the two groups has been running high for years. Ethnic Albanians are demanding political equality and their own university in Macedonia, where they say they represent around 40 percent of the population.
The government says census figures show the figure is around 22 percent and Albanian demands for stronger identity are fiercely opposed by Macedonian nationalists.
